title: AgentTraceLite
summary: Inspect OTLP JSONL traces offline and surface agent, model, tool, latency, error, and token signals without a tracing backend.
problem: Developers receiving OpenTelemetry traces from AI coding agents need a quick way to inspect a captured trace file without standing up a full tracing backend or uploading potentially sensitive telemetry.
audience: Developers experimenting with OpenTelemetry-enabled coding agents and local GenAI instrumentation.
why_now: GitHub announced OpenTelemetry support in the Copilot app on 2026-09-22, while OpenTelemetry defines a standard JSONL file serialization for OTLP telemetry.
difference: AgentTraceLite is a standard-library-only, read-only file inspector for quick local triage; it does not replace production tracing storage or dashboards.
monetization_hypothesis: Best kept as a free local utility; paid team features would require separate demand validation.
limitations: Trace JSONL only; no protobuf binary, metrics, or logs.
Heuristic categories depend on span names and semantic attributes.

alternatives.name: Jaeger
alternatives.difference: Jaeger provides a collector/query/UI tracing system; AgentTraceLite reads an existing JSONL trace locally with no service to run.

alternatives.name: Grafana Tempo
alternatives.difference: Tempo is a trace backend for ingestion, storage and querying; AgentTraceLite is a zero-backend file triage tool.
